title: Cities, Homes & Well-being
description: From your course: words for describing cities and homes, how places get changed and improved, and how green and blue spaces affect your well-being.

items.definition: places that are in or near towns and cities
items.example: Life in [urban areas] can be stressful, so I escape to the countryside most weekends.
items.exampleRu: Жизнь в городе бывает очень напряжённой, поэтому почти каждые выходные я сбегаю за город.
items.trap: 'Urban' sounds formal; in conversation people usually just say 'in cities' or 'in town'.

items.definition: happening or used inside a building
items.example: When it's raining, I go to the [indoor] pool instead of running.
items.exampleRu: Когда идёт дождь, я вместо пробежки хожу в крытый бассейн.
items.trap: 'Indoor' goes before a noun ('an indoor pool'); after a verb use 'indoors': 'stay indoors', not 'stay indoor'.

items.definition: happening or used outside, not in a building
items.example: In summer our gym runs [outdoor] classes in the park, which I love.
items.exampleRu: Летом наш спортзал проводит занятия на улице, в парке, и я это обожаю.
items.trap: Before a noun use 'outdoor' ('outdoor classes'); after a verb use 'outdoors' ('we trained outdoors'). «На улице» here is not 'street'.

items.definition: having plenty of light, so it is easy and safe to see
items.example: At night I take the longer way home, along [well-lit] streets.
items.exampleRu: Вечером я хожу домой более длинной дорогой — по хорошо освещённым улицам.
items.trap: Use 'lit', not 'lightened' (= made lighter in colour); the opposite is 'poorly lit' or 'dimly lit'.

items.definition: the place and things around you
items.example: Working from a café helps me focus — sometimes I just need a change of [surroundings].
items.exampleRu: Работа в кафе помогает мне сосредоточиться — иногда просто нужно сменить обстановку.
items.trap: Always plural: 'my surroundings'. It's about places; for the people around you («моё окружение») say 'the people around me'.

items.definition: on or near the coast, the land next to the sea
items.example: We're spending the weekend in a little [coastal] town in Cornwall.
items.exampleRu: Мы проведём выходные в маленьком приморском городке в Корнуолле.
items.trap: Spelt 'coastal' with 'oa' (ˈkəʊstl); 'costal' is a different word about ribs. 'A seaside town' is also very common in the UK.

items.definition: areas of grass and trees in a town, like parks
items.example: One thing I love about this neighbourhood is all the [green spaces] nearby.
items.exampleRu: Что мне нравится в этом районе — рядом много зелёных зон.
items.trap: Don't say 'green zones' (from «зелёные зоны»); 'green spaces' or just 'parks' is natural.

items.definition: areas of water in or near a town, like rivers, lakes, canals or the sea
items.example: Apparently living near [blue spaces] like rivers or the sea makes you happier.
items.exampleRu: Говорят, если жить рядом с водой — рекой или морем, — становишься счастливее.
items.trap: A term from research and the news; in everyday talk people usually say 'near water' or 'by the river'.

items.definition: the state of feeling healthy, comfortable and happy
items.example: Ditching the bus and walking to work has done wonders for my [well-being].
items.exampleRu: С тех пор как я хожу на работу пешком, а не езжу на автобусе, самочувствие стало заметно лучше.
items.trap: Uncountable: 'my well-being', not 'a well-being'. Also spelt 'wellbeing'.

items.definition: a person whose job is to study a subject carefully to find new facts
items.example: My cousin works as a [researcher] at a university lab in Manchester.
items.exampleRu: Мой двоюродный брат работает исследователем в университетской лаборатории в Манчестере.
items.trap: The work is 'research' (uncountable): 'do research', not 'make researches'; the person is a 'researcher'.

items.definition: to guess possible reasons or answers without knowing all the facts
items.example: People at work keep [speculating] about who'll replace our manager.
items.exampleRu: На работе все без конца гадают, кто займёт место нашего руководителя.
items.trap: In everyday English it means «гадать, строить догадки», not «спекулировать» (reselling); use 'about' or 'on', not a direct object.

items.definition: made dirty by smoke, chemicals or rubbish
items.example: Cycling to work would be great if the main road weren't so [polluted].
items.exampleRu: Ездить на работу на велосипеде было бы здорово, если бы главная дорога не была такой загазованной.
items.trap: 'Polluted' is the adjective, 'pollution' the noun: 'the air is polluted', 'air pollution'.

items.definition: a river or canal that boats can travel along
items.example: Walking along the city's [waterways] is my favourite way to clear my head after work.
items.exampleRu: Прогулка вдоль городских рек и каналов — мой любимый способ проветрить голову после работы.
items.trap: One word, and it means rivers and canals, not «водопровод» (that's 'water supply' or 'the water mains').

items.definition: a structure that pushes water up into the air, often in a park or square
items.example: Let's meet by the [fountain] in the main square at six.
items.exampleRu: Давай встретимся у фонтана на главной площади в шесть.
items.trap: Stress the first syllable, ˈfaʊntən, not 'fon-TAN' as in Russian; spelt '-tain'.

items.definition: to relax and stop feeling worried or tense
items.example: After a crazy week at work, I usually [de-stress] with a long walk by the river.
items.exampleRu: После сумасшедшей недели на работе я обычно снимаю стресс долгой прогулкой вдоль реки.
items.trap: It's a verb with no object: 'I de-stress', not 'take off stress' (from «снять стресс»); with a noun, say 'relieve stress'.

items.definition: to make someone feel full of energy again, or to bring something back to life
items.example: A quick swim in the lake first thing always [revives] me.
items.exampleRu: Утреннее купание в озере всегда возвращает меня к жизни.
items.trap: Say 'it revives me' or 'I feel revived', not 'I revive myself'; not 'reanimate' (that's for bringing the dead back).

items.definition: the main part of a city, where most shops and offices are
items.example: Parking in the [city centre] is a nightmare, so I always take the tram.
items.exampleRu: Парковаться в центре города — это кошмар, поэтому я всегда езжу на трамвае.
items.trap: British spelling 'centre' (US 'center' or 'downtown'); say 'in the city centre', not 'in the centre of city'.

items.translation: неиспользуемые, пустующие зоны города (вдоль улиц и набережных)
items.definition: unused areas along a street or river, like blank walls or empty buildings, where nothing happens
items.example: The council wants to turn the [inactive edges] along the canal into cafés and seating.
items.exampleRu: Муниципалитет хочет превратить пустующие участки вдоль канала в кафе и места для отдыха.
items.trap: A town-planning term; in everyday talk people say 'empty' or 'unused' areas. Use 'inactive', not 'unactive'.

items.definition: to completely destroy a building on purpose
items.example: They're [demolishing] the old shopping centre to build flats, so there's noise all day.
items.exampleRu: Старый торговый центр сносят, чтобы построить жильё, так что весь день стоит шум.
items.trap: «Сносить» a building is 'demolish', 'knock down' or 'pull down', not 'break' or 'ruin'.

items.definition: a very tall building with many flats or offices (UK)
items.example: The view from the fourteenth floor of our [tower block] is amazing at night.
items.exampleRu: Вид с четырнадцатого этажа нашей многоэтажки ночью просто потрясающий.
items.trap: UK English; a 'skyscraper' is much taller and usually offices. A 'multi-storey' in the UK is a car park.

items.definition: to change something so it is more modern and works better
items.example: We'd love to [modernise] the kitchen, but it'll cost a fortune.
items.exampleRu: Мы бы с радостью обновили кухню, но это обойдётся в целое состояние.
items.trap: British spelling '-ise' (US '-ize'); use the verb, not 'make a modernisation of sth'.

items.definition: to build something again after it has been damaged or destroyed
items.example: After the fire, they had to [reconstruct] the whole roof of our building.
items.exampleRu: После пожара пришлось заново отстраивать всю крышу нашего дома.
items.trap: It usually means rebuilding something damaged; for improving an old building, 'renovate' or 'refurbish' is more natural than «реконструкция».

items.definition: to change something completely, usually so it is much better
items.example: A few plants and a new rug have completely [transformed] my tiny flat.
items.exampleRu: Пара растений и новый коврик полностью преобразили мою крошечную квартиру.
items.trap: Use 'into', not 'to', for the result: 'transform an old warehouse into flats'.

items.definition: to join together and become one
items.example: Our two teams are [merging] next month, so I'll have a new manager.
items.exampleRu: В следующем месяце наши два отдела объединяют, так что у меня будет новый руководитель.
items.pattern: merge (with sth) / merge A and B / merge into sth
items.trap: Say 'merge with', not 'merge to'; don't confuse it with 'emerge' (появиться). The business noun is 'a merger'.

items.definition: the organisation that runs public services in a town or area (UK)
items.example: You should report the broken street lights to the [local authority] — they fix them quickly.
items.exampleRu: Про сломанные фонари лучше сообщить в муниципалитет — их быстро чинят.
items.trap: Sounds official; in everyday British English people just say 'the council'. Not 'local power' (from «местная власть»).

items.definition: to make something look cleaner, neater or more attractive
items.example: Let's [spruce up] the spare room before your parents come to stay.
items.exampleRu: Давай приведём в порядок гостевую комнату до приезда твоих родителей.
items.pattern: spruce sth up / spruce up sth
items.trap: Informal, for small quick improvements; bigger building work is 'refurbish' or 'renovate'.

items.definition: to repair and decorate a building or room so it looks new
items.example: The gym's closed for two weeks while they [refurbish] the changing rooms.
items.exampleRu: Спортзал закрыт на две недели — там делают ремонт в раздевалках.
items.trap: «Делать ремонт» is 'refurbish', 'renovate' or 'do up', not 'make repair'; 'repair' is for fixing something broken.

items.definition: to repair something old so it looks as it did originally, or to bring something back
items.example: That pub on the corner has been beautifully [restored], so let's try it on Friday.
items.exampleRu: Тот паб на углу красиво отреставрировали — давай сходим туда в пятницу.
items.trap: Not 'restaurate' (from «реставрировать»): the verb is 'restore' and the noun 'restoration'.

items.definition: to have a very big effect, usually a good one
items.example: Getting blackout curtains has [made a huge difference] to my sleep.
items.exampleRu: Плотные шторы очень сильно улучшили мой сон.
items.pattern: make a huge difference to sth/sb
items.trap: Use 'make', not 'do' or 'have', and 'to' for what changes: 'a huge difference to my sleep'.

items.definition: totally; in every way
items.example: Sorry, your message [completely] slipped my mind — I'll reply properly tonight.
items.exampleRu: Прости, твоё сообщение совсем вылетело у меня из головы — вечером отвечу нормально.
items.trap: Keep the 'e' of 'complete': 'completely', not 'completly'.

items.definition: thought to be true without checking or proof
items.example: Everyone [assumed] the meeting was cancelled, so nobody turned up.
items.exampleRu: Все решили, что встречу отменили, поэтому никто не пришёл.
items.trap: Don't confuse 'assumed' (thought without checking) with 'assured' (promised, заверил).

items.definition: the first of two things or people just mentioned
items.example: If it's a choice between pizza and sushi tonight, I'd go for [the former].
items.exampleRu: Если выбирать между пиццей и суши, сегодня я за первое.
items.pattern: A and B … the former (= A), the latter (= B)
items.trap: Only for two things, and a bit formal; in conversation 'the first one' is more common. 'Former' before a noun means previous: 'my former boss'.

items.definition: how right or acceptable someone or something is for a purpose
items.example: The interview is mainly to check your [suitability] for the role, so don't stress.
items.exampleRu: Собеседование нужно в основном для того, чтобы понять, подходишь ли ты на эту должность, так что не переживай.
items.trap: Formal; in conversation people say 'whether you're right for it'. Use 'for', not 'to'.

items.definition: a high desk you use while standing up
items.example: Since I got a [standing desk], my back hasn't hurt once.
items.exampleRu: С тех пор как у меня появился стол для работы стоя, спина ни разу не болела.
items.trap: The '-ing' form is fixed: 'a standing desk', not 'a stand desk'.

items.definition: a machine that cleans the air in a room
items.example: With my hay fever, an [air purifier] in the bedroom has been a lifesaver.
items.exampleRu: При моей аллергии на пыльцу очиститель воздуха в спальне — просто спасение.
items.trap: Don't confuse it with an 'air conditioner' (кондиционер), which cools the air.
